extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (patent attorneys/agents) and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining patent term adjustment (PTA) reductions, reinstatements, and extensions (including regulatory-review extensions), and what constitutes an application being in condition for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for request for suspension under § 1.103
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files a request for suspension of action under § 1.103, the period of adjustment set forth in § 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the date the request was filed and ending on the date of termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Days during the suspension requested by the applicant are excluded from PTA; reduction equals the span from filing the suspension request to termination of the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for deferral of issuance under § 1.314
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for deferral of issuance of a patent under § 1.314 causes a reduction of the period of adjustment by the number of days beginning on the date the request for deferral was filed and ending on the earlier of the date a request to terminate the deferral was filed or the date the patent was issued (in some rule-versions, ending on the date the patent was issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issuance is deferred at applicant's request, those deferred days are excluded from PTA; rule language varies slightly by effective-date versions—apply the version applicable to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for abandonment or late payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of the application or late payment of the issue fee results in reduction of PTA by the number of days beginning on the date of abandonment or the day after the issue fee was due and ending on the date a grantable petition to revive the application or to accept late payment of the issue fee was filed (or, in some versions, ending on the date of mailing of the decision reviving the application or accepting late payment, or four months after the grantable petition was filed, whichever is earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different historical rule versions apply to different application cohorts; reductions may stop at filing of a grantable petition or at revival decision; consult the version of § 1.704 applicable to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for failure to timely petition to withdraw holding of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive an application within two months from the mailing date of a notice of abandonment results in reduction of PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date two months from the mailing date and ending on the date a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive the application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not act within the two-month window following notice of abandonment, the days after that two-month mark until revival-petition filing are excluded from PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for conversion of provisional to nonprovisional (35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a provisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) to a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) causes reduction of PTA by the number of days beginning on the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) and ending on the date a compliant request to convert under § 1.53(c)(3) was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Days between initial provisional filing and the compliant conversion request are excluded from PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for late preliminary amendment or preliminary paper (near Office action/allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before the mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires mailing of a supplemental Office action or notice of allowance reduces PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date that is eight months from either the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or the date of commencement of the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371(b) or (f) and ending on the date the preliminary amendment or other paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late preliminary submissions that force supplemental actions lead to reduction measured from a defined eight-month reference date to the filing date of the preliminary paper; older rule-versions measure reduction as the lesser of the supplemental-action interval or four months—apply the applicable version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for reply having an omission (§ 1.135(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply having an omission (§ 1.135(c)) is filed, PTA is reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date the reply with omission was filed and ending on the date the reply or other paper correcting the omission was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time during which the record contains an incomplete reply (until corrected) is excluded from PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for submission of unsolicited supplemental reply or other paper after an initial reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper, other than one expressly requested by the examiner, after a reply has been filed reduces PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date the initial reply was filed and ending on the date the supplemental reply or other such paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unrequested supplemental filings that follow an initial reply will exclude the intervening days from PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for amendment after PTAB or Federal court decision (near Office action/allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or other paper after a decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (other than one designated as a new ground of rejection under § 41.50(b) or a statement under § 41.50(c)) or a decision by a Federal court, less than one month before the mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires mailing of a supplemental Office action or supplemental notice of allowance, reduces PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date of the decision and ending on the date the amendment or other paper was filed (or, in some historical versions, by the lesser of that interval or four months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-decision amendments filed close to an impending Office action/allowance that cause supplemental actions will exclude the days between decision and amendment filing; consult the applicable historical rule text for four-month caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for amendment under § 1.312 or other paper filed after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper (other than an amendment expressly requested by the Office or an RCE in compliance with § 1.114) after a notice of allowance has been given or mailed reduces PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the amendment or other paper was filed (or, in older rule-versions, measured as the lesser of that interval or four months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any non-requested amendments after allowance can reduce PTA; RCEs compliant with § 1.114 and Office-requested amendments are exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for failure to file appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months from the date a notice of appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board was filed results in reduction of PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date three months from the notice of appeal and ending on the date an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 or a request for continued examination in compliance with § 1.114 was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appeal brief is late, the intervening days until filing of a compliant brief or an RCE are excluded from PTA; different historical rule-versions apply depending on filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for submission of a request for continued examination (RCE) after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after any notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 has been mailed reduces PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE filed after allowance (rather than before) causes excluded days from PTA measured from the day after notice of allowance to the RCE filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for failure to provide application in condition for examination within eight months
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to provide an application in condition for examination as defined in paragraph (f) within eight months from either the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or the date of commencement of the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371(b) or (f) results in reduction of PTA by the number of days beginning on the day after the date that is eight months from those reference dates and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is not in condition for examination within the eight‑month window, days until the application becomes in condition are excluded from PTA; see paragraph (f) for what 'in condition for examination' requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'in condition for examination' (paragraph (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes: a specification with at least one claim and an abstract (§ 1.72(b)); papers in compliance with § 1.52; drawings (if any) in compliance with § 1.84; any required English translation (§ 1.52(d) or § 1.57(a)); a 'Sequence Listing' (if applicable) in compliance with §§ 1.821–1.825 or 'Sequence Listing XML' in compliance with §§ 1.831–1.835; an inventor's oath or declaration or an application data sheet containing the information in § 1.63(b); the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(a)/(c)), search fee (§ 1.16(k)/(m)), examination fee (§ 1.16(o)/(q)); any certified copy required by § 1.57(a); and any application size fee required by § 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications entering the national stage, analogous requirements and fees under § 1.492 apply. Papers/drawings/sequence listings corrected by the latest reply filed prior to mailing of an action or notice are considered compliant as of that latest reply's filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for further prosecution via continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: Further prosecution via a continuing application causes the period of adjustment set forth in § 1.703 to exclude any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods attributable to prosecution of an earlier-filed application (before the actual filing date of the patent-applicant application that resulted in the patent) are not included in PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-only filings not treated as failure if accompanied by timely statement (paragraph (d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement (IDS) in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution if the IDS (or an RCE containing only an IDS) is accompanied by a statement that each item of information was first cited in a communication from a counterpart foreign/international patent office or the Office and that the communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to filing the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30‑day period is non-extendable. For statements filed on or after July 17, 2023, the statement must be on PTO/SB/133 using document code PTA.IDS; presentation of that form constitutes certification under § 11.18(b) that the form text was not altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement not treated as failure to conclude prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced PTA will not itself be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under paragraph (c)(10) of § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the reinstatement request does not create additional PTA-reducing conduct under the cited paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent must indicate any PTA and timeline for reconsideration (§ 1.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent will include notification of any patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). Any request for reconsideration of the PTA indicated on the patent must be by way of an application for patent term adjustment filed no later than two months from the date the patent was granted (this two-month period may be extended under § 1.136(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application for reconsideration must be accompanied by the fee in § 1.18(e) and a statement specifying the correct PTA and the legal basis under § 1.702, the relevant dates per §§ 1.703(a)–(e), whether there is a terminal disclaimer, and whether any § 1.704 circumstances occurred (or that none occurred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requests for failures to reply within three months (§ 1.705(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement of all or part of the PTA reduced pursuant to § 1.704(b) for failing to reply within three months must be filed prior to issuance of the patent and must be accompanied by the fee in § 1.18(f) and a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that, despite all due care, the applicant was unable to reply within three months. The Office will not grant more than three additional months for each reply beyond three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing must convince the Director that 'all due care' was exercised; the time limit for filing the reinstatement request is non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No third-party submissions/petitions on PTA (§ 1.705(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: No submission or petition on behalf of a third party concerning patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) will be considered by the Office; such submissions will be returned or otherwise disposed of at the Office's convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the applicant/patent owner (or authorized agent) may make PTA adjustment/reconsideration requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for patent term extension due to regulatory review (§ 1.710 & § 1.720)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is eligible for extension of the patent term if the patent claims a 'product' (as defined) either alone or in combination, or a method of using or manufacturing such a product, and meets all other conditions and requirements of the subpart. 'Product' definitions include: (1) active ingredient of a new human drug/antibiotic/human biological product (including salts/esters) alone or in combination; (2) active ingredient of a new animal drug or veterinary biological product (with manufacturing-method restrictions) including salts/esters; (3) any medical device, food additive, or color additive subject to regulation under the FD&C Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires both the claim scope to meet the product/method definitions and satisfaction of additional conditions in § 1.720 (see next entry). Historical amendments and applicability dates may affect particular patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for extension of patent term (§ 1.720)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent may be extended if: (a) the patent claims a product/method as defined; (b) the patent term has not been previously extended (except certain exceptions); (c) an application for extension is submitted in compliance with § 1.740; (d) the product was subject to a regulatory review period as defined in 35 U.S.C. 156(g) before its commercial marketing or use; (e) the product received permission for commercial marketing or use and meets first‑in‑class or specified manufacturing/animal-use conditions; (f) the application is submitted within the sixty-day period beginning on the date the product first received permission for commercial marketing or use (with specific permutations for manufacturing-method patents or certain animal drug patents); (g) the term has not expired before submission; and (h) no other patent term has been extended for the same regulatory review period for the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully verify timing (60-day filing window), the 'first permission' requirements, and whether other patents have been extended for the same regulatory review period; different sub-cases apply (manufacturing-method claims, animal drug claims, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and signature requirements for extension applications (§ 1.730)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for extension must be submitted by the owner of record of the patent or its agent and comply with § 1.740. If submitted by the patent owner it must be signed by the patent owner (in compliance with § 3.73(c)) or by a registered practitioner on behalf of the owner. If submitted on behalf of the patent owner by an agent (e.g., a licensee), the application must be signed by a registered practitioner on behalf of the agent. The Office may require proof that the agent or registered practitioner is authorized to act on behalf of the patent owner or agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper signature authority and be prepared to supply proof of authorization if requested by the Office; unsigned or improperly authorized filings risk rejection or delay.
